summary:
An unfinished 3D Godot application that shows a list of all lunar missions that resulted in a touchdown on the Moon, crash or otherwise. Intended to show LOS to Earth, Sun with down sampled NASA heightmaps for precise LOS calculations. Horizon API is used for positions and LOS.

Scope addresses the challenge, showing previous lunar missions will make users notice patterns and try to derive why previous missions were in certain locations, Earth/Sun LOS are important. Terrain Elevation is also important. Date range for duration of mission.
details:
Tech debt stacked up while trying to finish before deadline, so it is basically non-functional.

Horizon API is called on every click that changes the camera position relative to the Moon globe. Not good.

A 3D Godot application that shows a list of all lunar missions that resulted in a touchdown on the Moon, crash or otherwise. Also shows the LOS to the Earth and how the terrain will be lit by the (invisible) sun by using the Horizon API.
The intention is to show the Earth LOS for radio communications, the Sun LOS for solar power generation and a terrain model for accurate LOS calculations and landing viability. Previous lunar sites also let users study patterns in decision making made over the years.

Terrain is made by using real elevation data from NASA stored locally. It is down sampled to fit in Godot import limits so it is only has ~1KM of accuracy for showing large elevation differences when inside craters etc. Terrain surface looks the same always.
